parsedVerdict.reasoning: Both services deal with loans, but the module doesn't use its abstractions consistently. LendingService gets its gateways (BookGateway, MemberGateway, LoanGateway) through its constructor and turns the records it loads into domain models. LoanHistoryService gets PrismaService through its constructor, but in note() it ignores that and creates a new PrismaClient. That bypasses its own abstraction: the two methods of one class write and read through different clients. LoanHistoryService also calls Prisma directly instead of going through a gateway and a domain model, unlike its sibling. Finally, both services copy the same in-memory ID-generation pattern (sequence/counter fields with a string prefix), so that rule lives in two places.

violations.message: note() creates `new PrismaClient()` instead of using the PrismaService passed to the constructor (this.db). That bypasses the class's own abstraction, and eventsOf() still uses this.db, so reads and writes go through different clients.

Calls Prisma directly (db.loanEvent.create/findMany) with an ad-hoc LoanEvent shape, while LendingService goes through gateways and domain models (Book, Member, Loan). The module doesn't reach storage in one consistent way.

In-memory ID generation (`private sequence` + `loan-${this.sequence}`) repeats the counter pattern in LoanHistoryService (`private counter` + `evt-${this.counter}`). The ID-generation rule should live in one place.
